Product development is so wild ...

You can have a very green / inexperienced team do amazing things (with the lightest amount of direction)

And a team filled with highly experienced ppl at a complete standstill

must be me ... but I much prefer anti-product-visions to product visions. What will we NOT be. What will this NOT turn into.

not sure why, but I think it is because most product visions fail to tell me anything surprising.

features come and go
promises persist

remember ... start the "timer" from the moment you dream up an idea, the CEO says "awesome", and it enters the collective mental backlog of the org....

and you'll find out that "development time" is really but a small % of the effort. Yet where people obsess obsess obsess.

The @henrikkniberg original is a work of art.

I respectfully add this “not like this...”

Pondering this almost a year later...

More than "waterfall" or "agile" or whatever.... what we're really talking about is the definition/boundaries of a team. And the decisions authority of the team as a whole, and for individual team members. https://twitter.com/johncutlefish/status/1315806382348615680/photo/1
Weird how people need data when they don’t want to do something, but use intuition when they want to be like Steve Jobs.

healthy use of sprints...
less healthy use of sprints...

This is a sneaky/good format if you're forced to do this kind of roadmap...

1) long list of things you're saying no to
2) a single key focus
3) a place for stuff you might optionally focus on given more support (and top priority on track)
4) coarse-grained H2

"Why are you using that metric?"

"It's a standard metric. Everyone tracks it."

"Why?"

"It goes on our dashboards. The board looks at it. Everyone."

"But does it tell you? When I see it change, what is happening?"
